name: Psychology (Min)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
Completing a minimum of 35 units in Psychology is required for the minor, including PSYCH 1 Introduction to Psychology and PSYCH 10 Introduction to Statistical Methods: Precalculus or a comparable statistics course. Advanced Placement (AP) credit may not be used toward the Psychology minor.
Independent study, research, and practice cannot be counted toward the minor. Summer quarter Psychology courses are not applicable toward the 35 units needed for the minor.
All courses used to fulfill the minor’s requirements must be taken at Stanford (courses taken outside of Stanford cannot be petitioned to count) and passed with a grade of C- or better, except for courses offered only on a satisfactory/no credit basis.

rules.name: Course Requirements
rules.desc: The minor must include three of ten core courses with a minimum of one from each of two areas and elective Psychology courses of at least three units each, totaling 35 units:

children.name: Elective Psychology Courses
children.desc:
The remaining unit requirements can be fulfilled through elective PSYCH courses.
These can include additional courses from Areas A and B and other electives.
An elective Psychology course is any PSYCH course offered for three units or more (excluding independent study, research, and practicum). There are three cognate courses from other departments that count towards the major as PSYCH elective units: BIO 150, PSYC 135, and PSYC 139.

children.name: Third core course (Area A or B)

grading: All courses towards the 35-unit requirement must be taken for a letter grade of C- or better, except for courses offered only on a satisfactory/no credit basis.
transferPolicy: All courses used to fulfill the minor’s requirements must be taken at Stanford. Courses taken outside of Stanford cannot be petitioned to count.
reviewNotes: You take PSYCH 1 and PSYCH 10, three core courses with at least one from each of Areas A and B, and electives of 3 or more units, for 35 units, each letter graded with a C- or better unless it is offered only S/NC. Electives are PSYCH courses or the cognates BIO 150, PSYC 135 and PSYC 139; independent study, research and practica do not count. A comparable statistics course in place of PSYCH 10 is moved in by hand, and the rules against AP credit, summer-quarter Psychology courses and courses taken elsewhere are checked by hand.
